sources.citation: Rubino, Carl. 2005. Utudnon, an Undescribed Language of Leyte. In Hsiu-chuan Liao & Carl R. Galvez Rubino (eds.), Current Issues in Philippine Linguistics and Anthropology: Parangal kay Lawrence A. Reid, 306-336. Manila: Linguistic Society of the Philippines and SIL Philippines.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing explicit. Sec. 1 Phonology (pp.306-310) gives only segmental inventory ('The phonemes of Utudnon are those of Standard Cebuano with the addition of the alveopalatal affricate [j]'), *l>y and *y>j changes, consonant alternations. No occurrence of the words stress/accent/length/penult/syllable in the whole paper. Accent is marked lexically with an acute on every cited form, falling on either the penult or the final syllable (bayáy 'house', háboy 'blanket', buyák 'flower', búyan 'moon'); no rule stated.
sources.venue: Current Issues in Philippine Linguistics and Anthropology: Parangal kay Lawrence A. Reid

tone.quote: The phonemes of Utudnon are those of Standard Cebuano with the addition of the alveopalatal affricate [j]. Both languages exhibit a three vowel system /i, a, u/ with phrase-final vowel lowering usually reflected in their orthographies

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Mentions Baybayanon/Utudnon only for subgrouping (Warayan, map code c11), mu- for <um>, *y > /j/; no stress statement for Baybayanon. Diss-wide transcription convention (fn.2 p.196): acute marks a stressed vowel.

sources.note: Nothing; states that Rubino 2005 is the only dedicated publication on the language; location (5 barangays of Baybay), ~10,000 population, Warayan affiliation.

sources.note: No Baybayanon/Utudnon sample point (Table 2 no. 21 'Leyte (Ceb)' is the Cebuano of central-western Leyte = Rubino's 'Leyteno', not bvy); its Bisayan accent sections therefore do not cover this language.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David (comp.). 2018. Utudnon = VOCABULARY = SORTED. Unpublished.docx, 18 pp., 394 entries (docx metadata: creator David Zorc, created and last modified 2018-12-15): the Utudnon forms and example sentences of Rubino (2005) re-sorted alphabetically and re-spelled in Zorc's phonemic orthography (o > u, glottal stop written), with Cebuano/Leyteno comparanda. Posted in Zorc's field-notes web folder RDzorc/Baybayanon=Utudnon=Haya/, zorc.net.
